title: Log redaction for relay and RPC errors, and whether to check existing logs and rotate the bloXroute header and RPC keys

options.name: Keep current behaviour: log whole error objects
options.risk: Every bloXroute relay failure writes the auth header, and every HTTP-level RPC error the RPC URL with its key, into the logs (AUD-TX-014); anyone who sees the logs can use them.

options.name: Add logger-level redaction (and log message/code only at these sites); no rotation
options.risk: Credentials already in old log files stay valid.

options.name: Redact, have the operator check old log files, and rotate the bloXroute header and RPC keys if any line contains them
options.behavior_impact: New logs clean and leaked values revoked.

recommendation: redact-and-rotate if BSC (bloXroute) was ever enabled or logs were ever shared; otherwise redact-only. Context (added at the 22-20 Task 3 close-out, supplied by the execute-phase orchestrator; not an operator ruling): the backup copies of the only persisted log files (data/bot-capture-21-07.log, data/capture-21-07.log, data/capture-21-07b.log) were covered by the operator's D-22 exact-value check, which found none of BLOXROUTE_AUTH_HEADER, ALCHEMY_URL or any set *_RPC_URL / *_WS_URL value (.planning/baselines/safe01-offmachine.json exact_value_check; AUD-TX-014 last evidence entry). So the "check old log files" step of redact-and-rotate is already done for persisted logs; what the rotation question still depends on is terminal output that was never saved, which cannot be checked.
default: Keep current behaviour until the owning phase decides (milestone contract); S2 EXPOSURE (credentials in logs), so the default may stand until then.
behavior_impact: Decides what error detail the logs keep and whether credentials are rotated.
needed_by: Phase 29 discussion (S2-S4 fixes); the operator may choose to check logs earlier
